Main article: [Philippine literature](/wiki/Philippine_literature "Philippine literature")

[![photograph of José Rizal](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c9/Jose_Rizal_full.jpg/250px-Jose_Rizal_full.jpg)](/wiki/File:Jose_Rizal_full.jpg)

José Rizal's writings inspired the [Philippine Revolution](/wiki/Philippine_Revolution "Philippine Revolution").

Philippine literature consists of [works](/wiki/Filipiniana "Filipiniana") usually written in Filipino, [Spanish](/wiki/Philippine_literature_in_Spanish "Philippine literature in Spanish"), or [English](/wiki/Philippine_literature_in_English "Philippine literature in English"). Some of the earliest well-known works were created from the 17th to the 19th centuries.[[667]](#cite_note-676) They include *[Ibong Adarna](/wiki/Ibong_Adarna "Ibong Adarna")*, an epic about an eponymous magical bird,[[668]](#cite_note-677) and *[Florante at Laura](/wiki/Florante_at_Laura "Florante at Laura")* by Tagalog author [Francisco Balagtas](/wiki/Francisco_Balagtas "Francisco Balagtas").[[669]](#cite_note-678)[[670]](#cite_note-679) [José Rizal](/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Rizal "José Rizal") wrote the novels *[Noli Me Tángere](/wiki/Noli_Me_T%C3%A1ngere_(novel) "Noli Me Tángere (novel)")* and *[El filibusterismo](/wiki/El_filibusterismo "El filibusterismo")*,[[671]](#cite_note-680) both of which depict the injustices of Spanish colonial rule.[[672]](#cite_note-681)

[Folk literature](/wiki/Philippine_folk_literature "Philippine folk literature") was relatively unaffected by colonial influence until the 19th century due to Spanish indifference. Most printed literary works during Spanish colonial rule were religious in nature, although [Filipino elites](/wiki/Ilustrado "Ilustrado") who later learned Spanish wrote [nationalistic](/wiki/Filipino_nationalism "Filipino nationalism") literature.[[231]](#cite_note-Rodell-2002-239): [59–62](https://books.google.com/books?id=y1CVR74_KHQC&pg=PA59) The American arrival [began](/wiki/Education_in_the_Philippines_during_American_rule "Education in the Philippines during American rule") Filipino literary use of English[[231]](#cite_note-Rodell-2

A prodigious talent as a teenager, Hamilton established himself as one of the world's best drivers following his record-breaking rookie year. Ko Wen-je was born in [Hsinchu](/wiki/Hsinchu "Hsinchu"), Taiwan, on August 6, 1959,[[6]](#cite_note-9) to Ho Jui-ying ([Chinese](/wiki/Traditional_Chinese_characters "Traditional Chinese characters"): 何瑞英) and Ko Cheng-fa ([Chinese](/wiki/Traditional_Chinese_characters "Traditional Chinese characters"): 柯承發; 1932–2025).[[7]](#cite_note-10) He has a younger brother and sister, both of whom earned doctorates in [information management](/wiki/Information_management "Information management") and [physiology](/wiki/Physiology "Physiology"), respectively.[[8]](#cite_note-11) His father, Cheng-fa, was an elementary school teacher who graduated from the [National Hsinchu University of Education](/wiki/National_Hsinchu_University_of_Education "National Hsinchu University of Education").[[9]](#cite_note-:18-12) His paternal grandfather, Ko Shih-yuan (柯世元), was a teacher who was arrested and tortured during the [February 28 incident](/wiki/February_28_incident "February 28 incident"),[[9]](#cite_note-:18-12) and died three years after.[[10]](#cite_note-13) His paternal great-grandfather, Ko Hsien-yin (柯賢蔭), was the manager of a Buddhist temple in [Baoshan, Hsinchu](/wiki/Baoshan,_Hsinchu "Baoshan, Hsinchu").[[11]](#cite_note-14)

In 1974, Ko began attending [National Hsinchu Senior High School](/wiki/National_Hsinchu_Senior_High_School "National Hsinchu Senior High School"), where four uncles and his brother had previously attended.[[12]](#cite_note-15) He won awards in multiple subjects— including mathematics, biology, chemistry, and English—and graduated in 1977 as class [valedictorian](/wiki/Valedictorian "Valedictorian").[[13]](#cite_note-16) In 1978, he enrolled at [National Yang-Ming University](/wiki/National_Yang-Ming_University "National Yang-Ming University") to study medicine,[[14]](#cite_note-17) but chose to resit the college entrance examinations and transferred to [National Taiwan University](/wiki/National_Taiwan_University "National Taiwan University") (NTU) in 1979.[[15]](#cite_note-18) He earned his [Bachelor of Medicine](/wiki/Bachelor_of_Medicine "Bachelor of Medicine") (M.B.) from NTU in 1986.[[16]]

Baldwin was raised by her grandparents and spent Saturdays with her mother, who suffered from mental illness and opioid addiction.[[6]](#cite_note-6) Her maternal grandfather, biochemist [David E. Green](/wiki/David_E._Green "David E. Green"), was [Jewish](/wiki/Jewish "Jewish") (the son of immigrants from Russia and Germany), and her maternal grandmother, who was [Anglican](/wiki/Anglican "Anglican"), was English-born.[[7]](#cite_note-7) Baldwin's aunt is biochemist [Rowena Green Matthews](/wiki/Rowena_Green_Matthews "Rowena Green Matthews"). Through her maternal grandfather, Baldwin is a third cousin of comedian [Andy Samberg](/wiki/Andy_Samberg "Andy Samberg").[[8]](#cite_note-8)[[9]](#cite_note-9)

Baldwin graduated from [Madison West High School](/wiki/Madison_West_High_School "Madison West High School") in 1980[[1]](#cite_note-bioguide-1) as the class [valedictorian](/wiki/Valedictorian "Valedictorian").[[10]](#cite_note-usatoday-10) She earned a [Bachelor of Arts](/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts "Bachelor of Arts") from [Smith College](/wiki/Smith_College "Smith College") in 1984 and a [Juris Doctor](/wiki/Juris_Doctor "Juris Doctor") from the [University of Wisconsin Law School](/wiki/University_of_Wisconsin_Law_School "University of Wisconsin Law School") in 1989.[[1]](#cite_note-bioguide-1)

Before entering state politics, Baldwin first held political office at age 24 when she was elected to the [Dane County](/wiki/Dane_County,_Wisconsin "Dane County, Wisconsin") [Board of Supervisors](/wiki/County_Board_of_Supervisors "County Board of Supervisors") in 1986. She served on the board until 1994.[[10]](#cite_note-usatoday-10) She also served one year on the [Madison](/wiki/Madison,_Wisconsin "Madison, Wisconsin") [Common Council](/wiki/City_Council "City Council") to fill a vacancy.[[11]](#cite_note-11)

Baldwin has worked as an attorney in private practice.[[1]](#cite_note-bioguide-1)

The facility generates power by utilizing 16 [turbines](/wiki/Water_turbine "Water turbine"), each with a generating capacity of 1.0 [GW](/wiki/Gigawatt "Gigawatt"), taking the generating capacity to 16,000 MW.[[18]](#cite_note-19) In terms of generating capacity, it is the second largest [hydroelectric](/wiki/Hydroelectric "Hydroelectric") power plant in the world, after the [Three Gorges Dam](/wiki/Three_Gorges_Dam "Three Gorges Dam").[[19]](#cite_note-20) It is estimated to generate 62.44 terawatt-hours ([TWh](/wiki/TWh "TWh")) annually and will save about 90 million tons of coal per year and consequently reduce annual carbon emissions by 248 million tonnes.[[7]](#cite_note-:4-8)

As of 2021, each of the 1,000 MW turbines are the biggest in the world. A turbine/generator assembly is 50 meters high and weighs 7,500 tons, and produces 24 k[V](/wiki/Volt "Volt").[[20]](#cite_note-horg-21)

The dam is supported by a [substation](/wiki/Substation "Substation") in [Butuo County](/wiki/Butuo_County "Butuo County") which converts the 500 kV AC generated to [800 kV DC for long distance transmission](/wiki/Ultra-high-voltage_electricity_transmission_in_China "Ultra-high-voltage electricity transmission in China"). In the book *The Ivory Tower and Harry Potter,* [Eliza T. Dresang](/wiki/Eliza_T._Dresang "Eliza T. Dresang") discusses Hermione's role in the series and its relationship to feminist debates. Dresang begins with an analysis of Hermione's name and the role of previous characters with the same name in mythology and fiction, and the heritage Hermione has inherited from these characters due to her name. Dresang notes the parallels between Hermione and Rowling, and asserts that Hermione's "compulsion for study" helps both the character's development, making Hermione "a prime example that information brings power", and the plot of the series, as her knowledge of the wizarding world is often used to "save the day". Dresang states that "Harry and Ron are more dependent on Hermione than she is on them." However, she adds that the frequency of Hermione's crying and hysteria is not believable based on her character, and is "quite out of line with her core role in the book."[[58]](#cite_note-Heritage-70)
